script: stop 1 card 2, answer 2: copies a Prep line word for word

findings.problem: The quotation drops the BSB's final period. Bible quotations must preserve the exact wording and punctuation.
The quotation drops the BSB's period after 'free.' Bible quotations must preserve the exact punctuation.

The cookie-payment joke does not click instantly. Being handed a cookie does not establish that it was free, so paying for it is not necessarily awkward. The comparison needs to establish an actual gift.
The quotation drops the BSB's final period. Bible quotations must preserve the exact punctuation.

The quotation beginning 'do not be encumbered' starts partway through a sentence without an ellipsis and drops its final period. The quoted fragment 'once more.' also adds a period where the BSB continues 'once more by a yoke of slavery.'
'So he's picking a picture everybody could feel' supplies Paul's reason for choosing the image and claims how everybody would receive it. The text does not state either.
The quotation beginning 'if you let yourselves' cuts into Galatians 5:2 without an ellipsis and omits its final period.
'That's why he signs his name first' adds an unstated reason and describes a signature the verse does not report. Paul identifies himself in the statement; the text does not say he signs it.
'Not a discount' introduces a joke on a card about circumcision. The heavy-moments rule excludes jokes on cards dealing with the body's private matters.
The quotation beginning 'if you let yourselves' cuts into Galatians 5:2 without the required ellipsis.
'That's why he puts his own name on the line' and 'He wants them to take this one seriously' supply a reason for Paul's self-identification that the text does not state.
The quotation beginning 'Christ will be' cuts into Galatians 5:2 without an ellipsis and omits the final period.
'He signs his name to it' turns Paul's self-identification into a reported signature. Galatians 5:2 does not say he signs this statement.
'Paul doesn't leave a middle shelf for this one' introduces a comic bakery image on a card about circumcision. Cards dealing with the body's private matters must have no joke.
The quotation 'is obligated to obey the whole law' cuts into Galatians 5:3 without an ellipsis and drops the verse's final period.
The full-verse quotation drops the BSB's final period.
'Take one piece and you've signed up for the whole batch' broadens Paul's specific statement about getting circumcised into a claim about taking any one piece of the law.
The 'whole batch' punchline introduces a joke on a card about circumcision. The heavy-moments rule excludes jokes on cards dealing with the body's private matters.
The quotation stops after 'Christ' without an ellipsis. In the BSB, the sentence continues with '; you have fallen away from grace.'
The quotation changes the BSB's semicolon after 'Christ' into a period and omits the rest of the sentence without an ellipsis.
Both 'have fallen away from grace' and 'have been severed from Christ' are cut from within Galatians 5:4 without the required ellipses. Their punctuation also does not preserve the BSB sentence.
'They drifted from it' substitutes gradual drifting for Paul's statement that they have fallen away from grace. The verse does not describe a gradual process.
The quotation begins after the BSB's opening 'But' without an ellipsis and drops the final period.

The quotation beginning 'by faith' omits the opening 'But' without an ellipsis and drops the final period. The embedded quotation 'severed from Christ' also cuts into Galatians 5:4 without marking the cut.
The quotation begins after the BSB's opening 'But' without an ellipsis and drops the final period.
The quotation 'What matters is faith expressing itself through love' drops the BSB's final period.
Both 'is obligated to obey the whole law' and 'faith expressing itself through love' cut into their source sentences without ellipses and omit the original sentence-ending punctuation.

'A man who takes it on' leaves out the condition in Galatians 5:3: getting himself circumcised. In context, the explanation applies that verse to 'keeping every command perfectly' instead of preserving Paul's stated condition.
The quotation omits the BSB's opening 'For' without an ellipsis and drops the final period.
The quotation drops the BSB's final period.
'He's asking who got in their way' adds a Bible fact from Galatians 5:7 without its reference. The explanation cites only Galatians 5:8.
The quotation drops the BSB's final period.
The quotation drops the BSB's final period.
The quotation drops the BSB's final period.

This explanation has only two complete sentences. 'No promotion here, friend' is a fragment and does not count toward the required three to five sentences. The Bible quotation also drops the BSB's final period.
The quotation begins partway through Galatians 5:11 at 'if I am still preaching' without the required ellipsis.

'I think Paul asks it because he is NOT preaching it' supplies a reason for Paul's question that the verse does not state. Marking it 'I think' does not override the rule against adding unstated reasons.
The quotation begins partway through Galatians 5:11 at 'if I am still preaching' without the required ellipsis.

'I think he asks it because he isn't preaching circumcision' supplies an unstated reason for Paul's question. The permission to mark guessed feelings as personal guesses does not permit guessed reasons.
The quotation omits the opening 'For' without an ellipsis and drops the period after 'flesh.'
The quotation omits the BSB's opening 'For' without the required ellipsis.
The Galatians 5:14 quotation omits the BSB's period after 'yourself.' The quotation 'serve one another in love' also cuts into Galatians 5:13 without an ellipsis and omits its final period.
The Galatians 5:14 quotation omits the BSB's period after 'yourself.' Also, identifying 'Remember the Sabbath day' as a command in the law adds a Bible fact without a reference for that command.
This explanation has only two complete sentences. 'A good command, friend, but not the one Paul picks' is a fragment. The Galatians 5:14 quotation also omits the BSB's period after 'yourself.'
The quotation omits the BSB's opening 'But' without an ellipsis and drops the final period.

'Biting and devouring ends with everybody eaten up' replaces Paul's conditional warning with an unconditional outcome and adds 'everybody.' Preserve the warning's 'if' and 'watch out, or' rather than declaring an inevitable result.
The quotation omits the BSB's opening 'But' without an ellipsis and drops the final period.

The quotation omits the BSB's opening 'But' without an ellipsis and drops the final period. The final sentence also refers to the instruction to serve one another in love without citing Galatians 5:13.

'The warning follows right after he says to serve one another in love' misstates the sequence. The instruction is in verse 13, and the decree about loving one's neighbor in verse 14 intervenes before the warning in verse 15.
